Base directory for this skill: <HOME>\repos\wiki-master\skills\wiki-ingest

Read [the shared core](../wiki-maintainer/SKILL.md) once per session.
Read [access and host commands](../wiki-maintainer/references/access.md) before touching the vault. Also read for this operation: [evidence](../wiki-maintainer/references/evidence.md), [operations](../wiki-maintainer/references/operations.md).
Load the rest only when this run reaches it — [efficacy](../wiki-maintainer/references/efficacy.md) before creating or merging a concept, alias or relationship; [maintenance](../wiki-maintainer/references/maintenance.md) when you compute the backlog with the content-hash join, or hit a structural repair.
Before the first authorized write, follow the shared operations completion contract; reuse existing session authorization.

If  is empty, find the backlog with the hash-join metric — run
`node "<absolute-plugin-root>/scripts/health.mjs" --backlog`. The **not ingested (no summary records
their hash)** list is the backlog; process those clippings. If it is `0`, nothing
is pending — stop and say so. (See the directly linked maintenance reference for
why this beats hand-diffing `tag:clippings` against `wiki/sources/`.)

**Open the operation first:** `node "<absolute-plugin-root>/scripts/op-begin.mjs" --op ingest`
This records what was already uncommitted, so the commit at the end contains your
work and not the user's in-progress writing. Close it in step 6.

**Keep the ledger as you go.** Record each page you write (`wiki/sources/...`, a concept
or synthesis you create or change) with
`node "<absolute-plugin-root>/scripts/op-ledger.mjs" add --since <token> <path>...`, and give
`--since <token>` to `index-gen.mjs` and `log-entry.mjs`. When this ingest follows a discover
run, take the clipping set from that run's ledger file (its `raw/clippings/...` entries), not
from `git show`. Delegated writers get the parent token in their brief and run the same `add`
for the pages they write; they never close the operation (see the operations reference).

Prefer a named clipping set; two concurrent ingests can overwrite shared concept
pages, so coordinate overlapping targets rather than processing the global backlog
in parallel. Update only pages substantively changed by the evidence.

Apply the [Reddit and Medium evidence policy](../wiki-maintainer/references/evidence.md#reddit-and-medium)
to every page you write: Reddit-derived content belongs under
`## Reddit discussion (anecdotal)` and Medium-derived content under
`## Medium articles`, including when updating a mixed-source page.

For each source:
1. Read the exact clipping through the guarded CLI or filesystem. Write derived
   Markdown through exact-path filesystem edits, never a whole CLI `content=` payload. Discuss
   the key takeaways with the user.
2. Write/update `wiki/sources/<slug>.md`: a summary with `sources: ["[[<raw link>]]"]`,
   `type: source`, `ai-generated: true`, and typed `created`/`updated`/`reviewed`.
   **Always quote each wikilink inside the list — `sources: ["[[A]]", "[[B]]"]`,
   never a bare `sources: [[A]]` or an unquoted block list (`- [[A]]`).** Both
   unquoted shapes look correct and Obsidian still renders the links, but neither
   is valid YAML: `[[A]]` is flow-sequence syntax one level too many and silently
   parses into a nested list instead of a string, which is exactly the "type
   mismatch, expected list" defect `node "<absolute-plugin-root>/scripts/repair-inline-sources.mjs"`
   exists to repair in bulk. Quoting is what makes it an unambiguous string.
   **Cite the clipping by its actual filesystem path — `sources: ["[[raw/clippings/<exact filename>.md]]"]` — copied from the path you just read, never retyped from
   the source's title.** The clipper slugifies a title into a filename (`/`, `:`,
   `#`, `*`, `?`, quotes and brackets all become `-`, then a 120-char cap), so any
   title carrying one of those characters or running long does NOT name its own
   file. Citing the remembered title produces a link to a file that does not exist:
   the page becomes a `provenanceGap` and its clipping reads as unparsed, even
   though the ingest itself was correct. List the resolved vault's exact `raw/clippings/` directory or reuse the path
   from step 1 rather than reconstructing it.
   Also record `source-hashes: [<sha256>, …]` — the `source-hash` frontmatter value
   of each clipping you summarized (read it from the clipping's frontmatter). This
   is the machine key the ingest-backlog metric joins on — immune to filename and
   citation drift; the `sources: ["[[…]]"]` wikilink stays for navigation.
   To repair vaults that already drifted this way:
   `node "<absolute-plugin-root>/scripts/repair-provenance-links.mjs"` (dry run) then `--apply`.
   **Figures.** If the clipping's frontmatter lists `figures:`, open each sidecar
   (`raw/figures/<slug>-p<N>.md`) and **look at the PNG with the Read tool** before
   writing. Embed the ones that carry evidence on the source page as
   `![[raw/figures/<slug>-p<N>.png]]` next to the claim they support, with a sentence
   saying what the figure shows (axes, series, trend) taken from what you see, not from
   the machine description. A page render is a whole page: say which part matters.
   Quote numbers read off a chart as approximate and attribute them. If the PDF has
   figures but no `figures:`, tell the user `clip-pdf.mjs --figures-only` can add them.
   Never edit or add to `raw/figures/`.
3. Before creating a concept, search the proposed title, equivalent wording and
   nearby passages. Extend the canonical page, add a genuinely equivalent alias,
   or explain the new concept's distinct scope. Use `_templates/concept-note.md`;
   follow the directly linked efficacy reference for aliases and relationships.
   Create a stub (`status: stub`) only for an identified gap. Explain each useful
   connection under `## Relationships`; keep supporting citations in `sources:`
   and the relevant prose. Relatedness does not establish support. Update the
   task map the new knowledge helps answer. Preserve `reviewed` on pages that
   received only metadata/link edits; stamp it only after factual verification.
4. Regenerate the catalog: `node "<absolute-plugin-root>/scripts/index-gen.mjs"`
   (never hand-edit index.md's generated fence). With another writer in the vault,
   add `--paths-file <ledger>` (the JSON array of pages this ingest wrote, from
   `op-ledger.mjs show --since <token> --out <ledger>`) so their
   uncommitted pages stay out of the catalog and their lines already in it stay in. Write the log entry by piping the
   narrative to `node "<absolute-plugin-root>/scripts/log-entry.mjs" --op ingest --title "<title>" --since <token>`
   (creates `log/<timestamp>-ingest-<slug>.md` in the resolved vault).
5. Never edit anything under `raw/`.
6. **Close the operation:**
   Run `op-ledger.mjs show --since <saved-token> --out <ledger>` and read what it lists as
   unclaimed (another writer's pages, or one of yours you did not record), then
   `node "<absolute-plugin-root>/scripts/op-commit.mjs" --op ingest --title "<what you ingested>" --since <saved-token> --paths-file <ledger>`
   Commits exactly the pages this ingest touched, as one revertable unit, and
   reports anything it deliberately left alone. Without `--paths-file` the close is refused while another operation is open. Then follow the shared completion contract to push your updates (`wiki-sync.mjs`, or `wiki-sync.mjs --op <saved-token> --paths-file <ledger> --title "<what you ingested>"` to close and push in one command) and verify remote publication. If the sync is refused because uncommitted edits overlap incoming changes (exit 3), read "Refused sync" in the [operations reference](../wiki-maintainer/references/operations.md): never reset, check out, stash or delete a file you did not write.

# Maintaining the wiki

Read this short core once per session. Obsidian is the wiki's IDE; Markdown is
its portable knowledge store. A failed app connection does not block supported
filesystem work. Load the directly linked references required by your operation,
not every reference for a simple lookup.

**Push the wiki updates you own.** An authorized wiki edit includes validation,
the scoped operation commit, and pushing to the configured upstream with
`wiki-sync.mjs`, followed by remote verification. Complete this without another
routine permission question unless the user explicitly says to hold publication
or keep the work local. A local commit or a closed token alone is not published.
Report a missing upstream or failed sync as unpublished work, with the next step;
preserve other writers' edits and tokens. See [operation completion](references/operations.md).

## Location and access

The vault is `WIKI_MASTER_VAULT`, default `~/.wiki-master-vault`; its Obsidian
name is `WIKI_MASTER_VAULT_NAME`, default the folder basename. Bundled helpers
resolve this through `scripts/lib/vault.mjs`. Start at this known root; do not
search the disk. Read the vault's own `AGENTS.md` and schema before changing it.

Read [access and host commands](references/access.md) before accessing the vault.
Use quoted absolute helper paths resolved from this installed skill directory
(two parents up is the plugin root), never from the user's current workspace.
Sibling skill names refer to their workflows; load `../<name>/SKILL.md` directly
when the host has no skill loader. Treat `` as the user's request when
not substituted by the host.

## Invariants

1. **Raw bodies are immutable.** Only clipping tools create `raw/` evidence;
   only pipeline tooling updates its frontmatter. Never move raw files to mark
   ingestion state. Never read, cite or count `.recycle/`; only purge owns it.
2. **Claims carry provenance.** Derived pages declare `sources: ["[[...]]"]`
   pointing to exact source/raw paths, and honest `ai-generated` authorship.
   Original `wiki/authored/` work explicitly declares `sources: []`.
3. **Verify against captured evidence.** Clippings outrank paraphrases or memory
   for what the vault holds, not for universal truth. Degraded captures cannot
   establish exact quotes; absence of support is not proof a claim is false.
   Cite answers; disclose contradictions and uncertainty rather than inventing.
4. **Keep three dates distinct.** `updated` means edited; `reviewed` means factual
   claims checked against evidence or current project behavior; index freshness
   means indexed content matches files. Mechanical edits preserve `reviewed`.
5. **Preserve scope and user work.** Reuse existing session authorization. Reads
   do not open operations, log, commit or refresh indexes. Before the first
   authorized write, follow [operation completion](references/operations.md).
   Resolve your own operation tokens automatically unless the user explicitly
   asks to leave them open; resume the same operation after recoverable failures.
   Never stage the whole vault. Purge retains its explicit plan approval.
6. **Keep Reddit and Medium separate.** In derived pages and query answers,
   place Reddit-derived material under `## Reddit discussion (anecdotal)` and
   Medium-derived material under `## Medium articles`. Preserve these sections
   when reusing wiki summaries. Follow the
   [Reddit and Medium evidence policy](references/evidence.md#reddit-and-medium).

## Layout and navigation

- `raw/clippings/`: evidence; `wiki/{sources,entities,concepts,syntheses,authored}/`:
  maintained pages; `moc/`: navigational maps; `log/`: one file per operation.
- Wiki frontmatter: `type` (source/entity/concept/synthesis/authored), `created`,
  `updated`, `reviewed`, `status` (stub/draft/maintained), `sources`, `ai-generated`.
- Use `[[wikilinks]]`; `![[embeds]]` are transclusion, not relationship edges.
  Write unwrapped logical lines; never split a wikilink across a line break.
- `index.md`'s generated catalog is derived: regenerate with `index-gen.mjs`;
  never hand-edit its fence or read-modify-write the file. Manual framing outside
  the fence is preserved. Prefer bounded search and relevant MOCs over loading
  the whole generated catalog.
- Treat search diagnostics as evidence about coverage, not relevance. A stale
  index can omit useful pages; read current passages and disclose weaker channels.
  Zero evaluated drift pages cannot establish that the wiki has no drift.

## Load only the relevant policy

| Operation | Direct references to read |
|---|---|
| Source claims, quotes, synthesis, editorial changes | [Evidence and page-type licenses](references/evidence.md) |
| Original project docs, guides, ADRs, backlog | [Canonical placement and living documentation](references/authoring.md) |
| Concepts, relinking, task maps, discovery, factual review | [Identity, relationships and verification](references/efficacy.md) |
| Ingest backlog, lint, structural repairs, migration | [Metrics, repairs and pattern limits](references/maintenance.md) |
| Domain workflow details when needed | [Workflow reference](references/workflows.md) |
| Any vault mutation | [Completion, logging, scoped commits and verified push](references/operations.md) |

Run cheap structural checks during substantive maintenance. A clean graph does
not establish factual correctness: sample changed or high-use pages when reviewing
knowledge. Skip an empty vault and avoid a full lint of an unchanged wiki.

1	# Completion for vault mutations
2	
3	Use this contract for every ordinary vault write, including standalone clipping,
4	authoring and applying triage decisions. Read-only search, query, health, freshness
5	and preview work do not open operations, log, commit or refresh indexes.
6	
7	**Own the update through verified publication.** An authorized wiki edit includes
8	validation, the scoped operation commit, and pushing to its configured upstream
9	with `wiki-sync.mjs`, followed by remote verification. Finish those steps without
10	asking a separate routine permission question. An explicit user instruction to
11	hold publication or keep the work local overrides this default. A local commit
12	or a closed token alone does not publish the update. If a remote is absent or sync
13	fails, report the work as unpublished with its exact next action. Never create a
14	remote or repository merely to satisfy this rule. A token is not resolved merely
15	because its file was deleted; account for the work and verify the outcome.
16	
17	1. **Resolve scope and authorization.** Read the vault's instructions. Existing
18	   session authorization counts: a request to make a wiki update includes its
19	   normal commit-and-sync completion unless an explicit hold applies. A request to
20	   answer/search does not authorize filing a new page. Purge requires its specific
21	   reviewed plan and publication approval; do not replace those with this rule.
22	2. **Open before the first write.** Run `op-begin.mjs --op <op>` and save its token.
23	   On task resumption, reconcile a saved token before opening another one. Keep
24	   the operation type, title, owned-path ledger, log path and last completed phase
25	   with it so recovery can distinguish unfinished work from an already closed step.
26	   It snapshots already-dirty paths; `op-commit` excludes them. It does not isolate
27	   simultaneous edits to the same file. Coordinate overlapping targets; preserve
28	   pre-existing changes and report exclusions instead of sweeping them into a commit.
29	   With concurrent writers, maintain an explicit ledger of the exact vault-relative
30	   files this operation owns, including its log and generated catalogs when safe.
31	   Let the writers keep it: give `--since <token>` to every clipper, to `log-entry.mjs`,
32	   to `index-gen.mjs` and to `refresh-catalogs.mjs --apply`, each of which records the
33	   exact path it writes (unquoted UTF-8, so a name with an em dash survives), and record
34	   a page you wrote with your own file tools using `op-ledger.mjs add --since <token>
35	   <path>...`. `op-ledger.mjs show --since <token> --out <file>` writes the JSON array
36	   `--paths-file` takes and lists on stderr what the close would get wrong: recorded
37	   paths that were already dirty before `op-begin`, recorded paths that are not dirty
38	   now, and changed paths nobody recorded (another writer's, or one you forgot; it
39	   never claims them). Do not rebuild the set from `git show` or `git status`: git
40	   prints a non-ASCII name in quotes with octal escapes unless told otherwise, and a
41	   name lost that way is lost without an error.
42	   Pass a JSON array of those paths using `op-commit.mjs --paths-file <file>`;
43	   keep the manifest under `.wiki-master/` or outside the vault. This narrows the
44	   newly dirty delta and reports other new paths as outside scope. A ledger path that
45	   was already dirty when you ran `op-begin` is refused, not skipped: `op-commit` exits 1,
46	   names it and keeps the token. If this operation wrote it, run the same `op-commit`
47	   again with `--include <path>` for each (or `--include-from <file>`); if another writer
48	   owns it, take it out of the ledger. **Create new files only after `op-begin`**: a page
49	   written first counts as already dirty. It does not isolate simultaneous edits to the
50	   same file.
51	   **The guard.** `op-commit` without `--paths-file` commits everything that became
52	   dirty since `op-begin`, which cannot tell this operation's new files from another
53	   open operation's. So while any other operation token exists, of any age (age cannot
54	   show that an operation was abandoned), such a close is refused: `op-commit: this
55	   close has no --paths-file and another operation is open: <token> (<op>), ...`. It
56	   exits 1, commits nothing, keeps the token, and prints the way out: `op-ledger.mjs
57	   show --since <token> --out <ledger>`, then the same `op-commit` with `--paths-file
58	   <ledger>`. There is no override flag. A close with `--paths-file` is unchanged, and
59	   with no other token open an unscoped close behaves as before. Every refused close
60	   (this one, a pre-dirty ledger path, an evidence mismatch) appends a counts-only
61	   line to `.wiki-master/op-refusals.jsonl`; see "Refusal record" below.
62	   When the ledger carries a receipt that records its own byte length and SHA-256
63	   (captured JSON or log evidence), also pass `--evidence-map <file>`: a JSON object
64	   of ledger path to `{ "bytes": N, "sha256": "<64 lower-case hex>" }`, kept beside
65	   the ledger. After staging and before committing, `op-commit` compares each staged
66	   blob with its declaration. On a mismatch it commits nothing, unstages, keeps the
67	   token, and names the file, the declared and stored size and hash, and the exact
68	   `.gitattributes` line (`<path> -text`) that keeps the bytes. Add that one line,
69	   list `.gitattributes` in the ledger and rerun. It never edits an attribute itself,
70	   and ordinary Markdown keeps the vault's text policy. A pass is reported as its own
71	   `evidence:` line, separate from the index notice.
72	   An existing enclosing operation may own delegated clips and triage bookkeeping;
73	   record who closes it rather than opening a second operation unnecessarily.
74	3. **Edit and validate.** Check the requested behavior/content, valid frontmatter,
75	   canonical placement and exact citation/link targets. Preserve raw bodies and
76	   unrelated changes. `reviewed` advances only for factual verification. On uncertain
77	   write timeouts inspect the target before retrying; do not make a duplicate page.
78	4. **Refresh affected catalogs once.** For project authoring run `node "<absolute-plugin-root>/scripts/refresh-catalogs.mjs" --project <slug> --apply` instead of three separate generators. It builds one vault graph, updates only that project's backlog and MOC, then the global index; unchanged files are not rewritten. 82	   operation vocabulary (ingest, discover, query, lint, relink); authoring uses
83	   relink. Never append to a shared aggregate log; browse through `log.base`. Pass
84	   `--since <token>`: the entry's name carries a timestamp known only now, and the
85	   ledger is how it reaches the close.
86	6. **Commit and inspect.** Run `op-ledger.mjs show --since <token> --out <ledger>`,

88	   --since <token> --paths-file <ledger>`. Without `--paths-file` the close is refused
89	   while any other operation is open (the guard, step 2). Verify its result and the actual changed paths. Never `git add -A`.

91	   for missing backends, skipped work or partial builds. A commit does not establish
92	   index freshness. Report a non-git vault as local-only; do not claim a commit.
93	7. **Push and verify your update.** `op-commit` itself never pushes. The plugin
94	   scripts own the vault's git, so sync with `node "<absolute-plugin-root>/scripts/wiki-sync.mjs"`,

97	   fetch. Run it after `op-commit`, never between edits; it names any operation still
98	   open. A conflict aborts the rebase, exits 1 and names the files; the local commits are
99	   intact. Report it and stop: do not force, resolve by guessing, or claim success.

102	   a lock, and run `wiki-sync` again. The line gives the lock's age; git records no holder,
103	   so a lock that stays old with no git process running is for the owner to judge.
104	   Older versions printed a held lock as a conflict in "unknown files": an empty file list
105	   means it was not a content conflict. Any sync, yours or another writer's, stashes and
106	   restores every uncommitted tracked file, so their modification times change and a CRLF
107	   file can come back LF with git's content unchanged; check line endings and content
108	   just before `op-commit`, not before an earlier sync.
109	   Inspect the sync result and verify the operation's resulting commit is included
110	   in the freshly fetched upstream. After a rebase, identify it by its unique log
111	   path and verify its actual changed paths rather than assuming its old SHA.
112	   Do not stop at a local commit, delegate publication to Obsidian Git, or ask the
113	   user to push work you are responsible for. Inspect outgoing commits first;
114	   coordinate rather than publish unrelated or explicitly held local commits.
115	   `--commit-local` first commits hand edits made outside any operation (the owner's
116	   own Obsidian edits) in one scoped `sync:` commit; it refuses while any operation is
117	   open, because dirty files cannot then be attributed. Use ordinary sync for your
118	   operation; do not use `--commit-local` to sweep another writer's unfinished work.
119	   When the user explicitly holds publication, retain the local commit and report
120	   that it is unpushed. Without an upstream, report local-only completion.
121	
122	   **Close and publish in one command.** `wiki-sync.mjs --op <token>` closes that one
123	   operation through the same close `op-commit` makes, then runs the normal sync and
124	   verifies against a fresh fetch. The scope is `--paths-file <ledger>` when given;
125	   otherwise the paths the operation's writers recorded (`op-ledger.mjs`), when it has
126	   any; otherwise an unscoped close, which the guard refuses while another operation
127	   is open. `--title "<title>"` is the commit message (default `published with
128	   wiki-sync --op`; the subject is `<op>: <title>`). It never closes a token it was not
129	   given, and it cannot be combined with `--commit-local` (a usage error, exit 1).
130	   Success prints `closed operation <token>: committed <sha7> (<n> file(s))`, then the
131	   normal sync lines, exit 0. After a landed close it prints the same hard-wrapped
132	   wikilink warning `op-commit` does and refreshes the semantic index. A refused or
133	   failed close (token not open, unreadable `--paths-file`, the guard, a pre-dirty
134	   path, a git failure) prints a line starting `not committed:` to stderr, exits 1,
135	   pushes nothing and keeps the token. A close that landed whose sync then failed
136	   prints a line starting `committed, not published:` with the short sha, exits 1, and
137	   the token is gone because the commit exists; run `wiki-sync.mjs` again once the
138	   cause is fixed. Pass `--paths-file` instead of relying on the recorded paths when
139	   you have also written pages with tools that do not record them.
140	
141	   Without `--op`, `wiki-sync` also prints, for each open operation that has recorded
142	   paths still uncommitted, `operation <token> (<op>) has <n> recorded path(s) not
143	   committed; if it is yours, close and publish it with: node scripts/wiki-sync.mjs
144	   --op <token>`. It is a line, not a failure: a sync cannot know whose operation it
145	   is, so the exit code is unchanged and already-committed work is still pushed. It
146	   follows the once-per-set, once-a-day rule of the open-operations note, keyed by
147	   token and recorded count, so it is said again when an operation records more. An
148	   open operation with no recorded paths gets only the existing note.

150	## Recovery and token ownership
151	
152	- **Retry the same operation.** After a recoverable failure, inspect the token,
153	  exact owned files and actual commits before retrying the failed step. Resolve
154	  an understood cause within the authorized scope without another confirmation.
155	  A failed Git close keeps its token; retry that `op-commit`, not the edits or an
156	  already-written log. Never delete a Git lock or guess at a content conflict.
157	- **Reconcile uncertain completion.** A timeout may have occurred after a commit
158	  or token removal. Verify the actual commit's subject and path membership, owned
159	  content and validation state. A completed no-op or already-committed operation
160	  with a retained token still closes through its own scoped `op-commit`; an empty
161	  delta alone does not prove completion. If the token is already gone, verify
162	  closure and continue from the next unfinished step rather than opening a new
163	  token or replaying work. After a sync rebase, locate the operation through its
164	  unique log path and recheck the resulting commit instead of relying on its old SHA.
165	- **Respect holds and ownership.** Do not close a user-held operation. A delegated
166	  worker reports its owned paths and validation to its enclosing operation's named
167	  owner rather than closing the parent's token. The hand-off is the ledger: the brief
168	  gives the worker the parent's token; the worker records each path it writes with
169	  `op-ledger.mjs add --since <parent token> <path>...` (a clipper it runs takes
170	  `--since` too) and reports its validation; it never runs `op-commit` or `op-abort`.
171	  The owner runs `op-ledger.mjs show --since <parent token>`, resolves whatever it
172	  lists as unclaimed, and closes once. That owner remains responsible for
173	  the scoped commit, push and remote verification; delegation does not drop the
174	  publication step. Leave other agents' tokens alone unless ownership was explicitly transferred;
175	  tokens contain an opening dirty-path snapshot, not proof of who owns later edits.
176	- **Leave actionable blockers.** If safe progress requires an unresolved conflict,
177	  missing authorization or another owner's action, retain the operation and record
178	  its token, owned paths, completed steps, pending work and exact next action. Report
179	  that blocker or ownership handoff; do not claim completion or silently abandon it.
180	
181	**Abandoned tokens.** List retained tokens with
182	`node "<absolute-plugin-root>/scripts/op-cleanup.mjs"` (a dry run). Older than 24
183	hours means a review candidate, not proven abandonment; these tokens still block
184	`wiki-sync --commit-local`. For a verified-abandoned operation you own, with no
185	unfinished work or user hold, apply cleanup with its explicit `--apply --token <id>`

187	can be completed. `--hours <n>` changes the age filter, with a one-hour minimum;
188	respect that eligibility and verify removal. Never sweep tokens by age or delete
189	them manually. Token files are local Git-ignored state, not cross-machine locks.
190	The paths an operation's writers recorded sit in `<token>.paths.jsonl` beside the
191	token. `op-commit` (when the close lands), `op-abort` and a stale token removed by
192	`op-cleanup` take it with them; `op-cleanup` also lists a ledger whose token is
193	already gone and removes it only with `--apply --token <that id>`.
194	
195	**Stopping early.** A session that opened an operation and will not finish it, or whose work landed another way, drops its own token with `node "<absolute-plugin-root>/scripts/op-abort.mjs" --since <token>`. It removes that one token whatever its age and nothing else: the files the operation wrote stay in the working tree, uncommitted, for a later operation to commit. Open operations are visible without running a sync: `health` and `session-brief` print a line when any are open, and `wiki-sync` mentions other writers' operations once for a given set of tokens, again when the set changes, and once a day while it stays true.
196	
197	**Refused sync.** `wiki-sync` refuses to integrate while uncommitted edits overlap files
198	that the upstream changed: it prints `uncommitted edits overlap incoming changes in
199	<files>` and exits 3, the one exit code for this refusal (every other failure exits 1).
200	It changes nothing: no commit, stash or checkout, and the files and open tokens are
201	untouched. With no operation open the dirty files are hand edits, and the message is that
202	one line ending `commit them (or finish the operation) and sync again`. With an operation
203	open the message is longer: one line per overlapping file, `<file>: recorded by operation
204	<token> (<op>)` when an open operation's recorded ledger names the file and it is still
205	dirty, otherwise `<file>: not recorded by any open operation`; then `Open operations:
206	<token> (<op>), ...`; then `If you wrote these edits, finish your operation
207	(wiki-sync.mjs --op <token>) and sync again.` (the token is filled in only when exactly one
208	open operation recorded an overlapping file, otherwise the line shows the literal
209	`<token>`); then `If you did not, leave them exactly as they are:
210	do not reset, checkout, stash or delete them. Wait for their owner to close the operation, then sync again.` That
211	last instruction is the rule: a file you did not write is not yours to reset, check out,
212	stash or delete to get the sync through. Wait, and sync again after its owner closes. The
213	`recorded by` line is a hint, not proof of ownership. It reads only what writers recorded
214	with `--since` or `op-ledger.mjs add` (a generated file such as `index.md` is recorded only
215	when `index-gen` ran with `--since`) and ignores a ledger path that is not dirty now, an
216	unreadable ledger and the opening snapshot in a token, which says what was already dirty,
217	not who wrote it. `not recorded by any open operation` therefore does not mean no one is
218	writing the file. Each refusal also appends a counts-only line to the refusal record below.
219

221	`wiki-sync` that stops on an overlap (see "Refused sync"), appends

226	`paths` is the size of the evidence map), `unscoped` (the guard; `paths` is how many

234	sits outside the defect count. The file is never trimmed by the plugin and a line that is
235	not a record of a known kind counts as nothing.
236	
237	**Git ownership.** The plugin's scripts make the scoped commits and the sync: `op-commit`
238	commits what one operation wrote, and `wiki-sync.mjs` pulls, rebases and pushes. A new
239	vault's `vault-schema.md` (written by `wiki-init`) carries the same statement; an existing
240	vault keeps its own file. The Obsidian Git plugin stays installed for its source-control
241	view and for pulling. Its auto-commit and auto-push must be off (auto commit-and-sync
242	interval 0, commit on file change off, auto push interval 0): they commit half-finished
243	operation edits under "vault backup" and leave `op-commit` an empty delta. `wiki-sync`
244	warns when they are on. Every machine sharing the vault needs the same setting. An
245	instruction elsewhere that says Obsidian Git is the sync engine is stale.
246	
247	**Done only when** the requested change is validated, applicable catalogs and one
248	operation log are recorded, the operation commit is verified (or its precise
249	limitation reported), and its push and remote publication are verified. A user-held
250	or local-only result must be labeled accordingly. If blocked partway, preserve the
251	actual operation/commit state and leave the actionable handoff above; a sync failure
252	after token closure does not require a replacement token. Do not start over blindly.
253	
254	## Exceptions with their own transaction
255	
256	**Re-clipping:** `apply-reclips.mjs` applies repairs but does not own a commit. Use an enclosing operation with an exact target list and ownership ledger; inspect its returned changed paths. 257	
258	- `purge.mjs --apply`, `--restore` and `--reconcile` own their manifests, logs and
259	  commits. Do not wrap their transaction in a competing commit. Collateral Markdown
260	  repairs use an ordinary operation after the purge commit. Keep every seed/plan,
261	  blocking-source and publication safeguard in the purge skill.
262	- Fresh `wiki-init` can open an operation before scaffolding: the helper can create
263	  its state directory before the other folders exist. Without Git, explicitly report
264	  local-only initialization; do not manufacture a repository or publish it.
265	- Starting triage UI only creates machine-local session state; it is not a content
266	  edit and does not need a commit. Applying dispositions that change tracked vault
267	  content or pipeline state uses an enclosing or new ordinary operation.
268	
269	## Executable lifecycle templates
270	
271	Replace absolute path placeholders, title and narrative with the real task. The
272	comment marks where the already-authorized edits and checks occur; do not run the
273	close step after a failed edit/check. These examples assume a configured upstream
274	and no explicit user hold, so they include the push step. For an explicit local-only
275	request, omit that step and report the unpushed commit. The close is scoped with
276	`--paths-file`; to close and publish in one command, replace the `op-commit` and
277	`wiki-sync` lines with `wiki-sync.mjs --op <token> --title 'Task title'` (add
278	`--paths-file <ledger>` to scope it explicitly).

283	  $env:WIKI_MASTER_VAULT = 'C:/absolute/path/to/vault'
284	  $wikiOpToken = node 'C:/absolute/installed/plugin/scripts/op-begin.mjs' --op relink
285	  if ($LASTEXITCODE -ne 0) { throw 'Could not open wiki operation' }

287	  # Record each page written with your own file tools: op-ledger.mjs add --since $wikiOpToken <path>...

# Completion for vault mutations

Use this contract for every ordinary vault write, including standalone clipping,
authoring and applying triage decisions. Read-only search, query, health, freshness
and preview work do not open operations, log, commit or refresh indexes.

**Own the update through verified publication.** An authorized wiki edit includes
validation, the scoped operation commit, and pushing to its configured upstream
with `wiki-sync.mjs`, followed by remote verification. Finish those steps without
asking a separate routine permission question. An explicit user instruction to
hold publication or keep the work local overrides this default. A local commit
or a closed token alone does not publish the update. If a remote is absent or sync
fails, report the work as unpublished with its exact next action. Never create a
remote or repository merely to satisfy this rule. A token is not resolved merely
because its file was deleted; account for the work and verify the outcome.

1. **Resolve scope and authorization.** Read the vault's instructions. Existing
   session authorization counts: a request to make a wiki update includes its
   normal commit-and-sync completion unless an explicit hold applies. A request to
   answer/search does not authorize filing a new page. Purge requires its specific
   reviewed plan and publication approval; do not replace those with this rule.
2. **Open before the first write.** Run `op-begin.mjs --op <op>` and save its token.
   On task resumption, reconcile a saved token before opening another one. Keep
   the operation type, title, owned-path ledger, log path and last completed phase
   with it so recovery can distinguish unfinished work from an already closed step.
   It snapshots already-dirty paths; `op-commit` excludes them. It does not isolate
   simultaneous edits to the same file. Coordinate overlapping targets; preserve
   pre-existing changes and report exclusions instead of sweeping them into a commit.
   With concurrent writers, maintain an explicit ledger of the exact vault-relative
   files this operation owns, including its log and generated catalogs when safe.
   Let the writers keep it: give `--since <token>` to every clipper, to `log-entry.mjs`,
   to `index-gen.mjs` and to `refresh-catalogs.mjs --apply`, each of which records the
   exact path it writes (unquoted UTF-8, so a name with an em dash survives), and record
   a page you wrote with your own file tools using `op-ledger.mjs add --since <token>
   <path>...`. `op-ledger.mjs show --since <token> --out <file>` writes the JSON array
   `--paths-file` takes and lists on stderr what the close would get wrong: recorded
   paths that were already dirty before `op-begin`, recorded paths that are not dirty
   now, and changed paths nobody recorded (another writer's, or one you forgot; it
   never claims them). Do not rebuild the set from `git show` or `git status`: git
   prints a non-ASCII name in quotes with octal escapes unless told otherwise, and a
   name lost that way is lost without an error.
   Pass a JSON array of those paths using `op-commit.mjs --paths-file <file>`;
   keep the manifest under `.wiki-master/` or outside the vault. This narrows the
   newly dirty delta and reports other new paths as outside scope. A ledger path that
   was already dirty when you ran `op-begin` is refused, not skipped: `op-commit` exits 1,
   names it and keeps the token. If this operation wrote it, run the same `op-commit`
   again with `--include <path>` for each (or `--include-from <file>`); if another writer
   owns it, take it out of the ledger. **Create new files only after `op-begin`**: a page
   written first counts as already dirty. It does not isolate simultaneous edits to the
   same file.
   **The guard.** `op-commit` without `--paths-file` commits everything that became
   dirty since `op-begin`, which cannot tell this operation's new files from another
   open operation's. So while any other operation token exists, of any age (age cannot
   show that an operation was abandoned), such a close is refused: `op-commit: this
   close has no --paths-file and another operation is open: <token> (<op>), ...`. It
   exits 1, commits nothing, keeps the token, and prints the way out: `op-ledger.mjs
   show --since <token> --out <ledger>`, then the same `op-commit` with `--paths-file
   <ledger>`. There is no override flag. A close with `--paths-file` is unchanged, and
   with no other token open an unscoped close behaves as before. Every refused close
   (this one, a pre-dirty ledger path, an evidence mismatch) appends a counts-only
   line to `.wiki-master/op-refusals.jsonl`; see "Refusal record" below.
   When the ledger carries a receipt that records its own byte length and SHA-256
   (captured JSON or log evidence), also pass `--evidence-map <file>`: a JSON object
   of ledger path to `{ "bytes": N, "sha256": "<64 lower-case hex>" }`, kept beside
   the ledger. After staging and before committing, `op-commit` compares each staged
   blob with its declaration. On a mismatch it commits nothing, unstages, keeps the
   token, and names the file, the declared and stored size and hash, and the exact
   `.gitattributes` line (`<path> -text`) that keeps the bytes. Add that one line,
   list `.gitattributes` in the ledger and rerun. It never edits an attribute itself,
   and ordinary Markdown keeps the vault's text policy. A pass is reported as its own
   `evidence:` line, separate from the index notice.
   An existing enclosing operation may own delegated clips and triage bookkeeping;
   record who closes it rather than opening a second operation unnecessarily.
3. **Edit and validate.** Check the requested behavior/content, valid frontmatter,
   canonical placement and exact citation/link targets. Preserve raw bodies and
   unrelated changes. `reviewed` advances only for factual verification. On uncertain
   write timeouts inspect the target before retrying; do not make a duplicate page.
4. **Refresh affected catalogs once.** For project authoring run `node "<absolute-plugin-root>/scripts/refresh-catalogs.mjs" --project <slug> --apply` instead of three separate generators. It builds one vault graph, updates only that project's backlog and MOC, then the global index; unchanged files are not rewritten. Leave out `--apply` for a dry run: it writes nothing and its `changed` list is the list an apply would change, and `--diff` prints each changed file's removed and added lines to stderr. With concurrent writers, pass `--paths-file <JSON ownership ledger>` so another writer's uncommitted pages stay out: a page is listed when it is in the last commit or the ledger names it, and a page another writer has only staged is not. A line the catalog already has for such a page, put there by that writer's own run, is kept. Inspect the returned `changed` paths; with `--since <token>`, an `--apply` records them in the operation's ledger (a dry run records nothing). Without a project selector it refreshes all projects. Standalone generators remain available and the project generators accept `--project`. A global scan is still needed for cross-project ambiguous names.
5. **Log once.** Pipe a concise narrative into `log-entry.mjs --op <op> --title
   "<title>"`. It writes one uniquely named `log/YYYY-MM-DD-HHmmss-<op>-<slug>.md`,
   with date/op/title frontmatter and a grep-friendly heading. Use the existing
   operation vocabulary (ingest, discover, query, lint, relink); authoring uses
   relink. Never append to a shared aggregate log; browse through `log.base`. Pass
   `--since <token>`: the entry's name carries a timestamp known only now, and the
   ledger is how it reaches the close.
6. **Commit and inspect.** Run `op-ledger.mjs show --since <token> --out <ledger>`,
   read what it lists as unclaimed, then `op-commit.mjs --op <op> --title "<title>"
   --since <token> --paths-file <ledger>`. Without `--paths-file` the close is refused
   while any other operation is open (the guard, step 2). Verify its result and the actual changed paths. Never `git add -A`.
   The helper attempts a semantic index refresh after committing; inspect notices
   for missing backends, skipped work or partial builds. A commit does not establish
   index freshness. Report a non-git vault as local-only; do not claim a commit.
7. **Push and verify your update.** `op-commit` itself never pushes. The plugin
   scripts own the vault's git, so sync with `node "<absolute-plugin-root>/scripts/wiki-sync.mjs"`,
   not a bare `git push`: it fetches, rebases onto the upstream (never a merge commit),
   pushes, retries once when another machine pushed first, and verifies against a fresh
   fetch. Run it after `op-commit`, never between edits; it names any operation still
   open. A conflict aborts the rebase, exits 1 and names the files; the local commits are
   intact. Report it and stop: do not force, resolve by guessing, or claim success.
   `rebase-failed` is different: the rebase never started (usually a held `.git/index.lock`),
   so no files are named and nothing changed. Wait for the other git process, never delete
   a lock, and run `wiki-sync` again. The line gives the lock's age; git records no holder,
   so a lock that stays old with no git process running is for the owner to judge.
   Older versions printed a held lock as a conflict in "unknown files": an empty file list
   means it was not a content conflict. Any sync, yours or another writer's, stashes and
   restores every uncommitted tracked file, so their modification times change and a CRLF
   file can come back LF with git's content unchanged; check line endings and content
   just before `op-commit`, not before an earlier sync.
   Inspect the sync result and verify the operation's resulting commit is included
   in the freshly fetched upstream. After a rebase, identify it by its unique log
   path and verify its actual changed paths rather than assuming its old SHA.
   Do not stop at a local commit, delegate publication to Obsidian Git, or ask the
   user to push work you are responsible for. Inspect outgoing commits first;
   coordinate rather than publish unrelated or explicitly held local commits.
   `--commit-local` first commits hand edits made outside any operation (the owner's
   own Obsidian edits) in one scoped `sync:` commit; it refuses while any operation is
   open, because dirty files cannot then be attributed. Use ordinary sync for your
   operation; do not use `--commit-local` to sweep another writer's unfinished work.
   When the user explicitly holds publication, retain the local commit and report
   that it is unpushed. Without an upstream, report local-only completion.

   **Close and publish in one command.** `wiki-sync.mjs --op <token>` closes that one
   operation through the same close `op-commit` makes, then runs the normal sync and
   verifies against a fresh fetch. The scope is `--paths-file <ledger>` when given;
   otherwise the paths the operation's writers recorded (`op-ledger.mjs`), when it has
   any; otherwise an unscoped close, which the guard refuses while another operation
   is open. `--title "<title>"` is the commit message (default `published with
   wiki-sync --op`; the subject is `<op>: <title>`). It never closes a token it was not
   given, and it cannot be combined with `--commit-local` (a usage error, exit 1).
   Success prints `closed operation <token>: committed <sha7> (<n> file(s))`, then the
   normal sync lines, exit 0. After a landed close it prints the same hard-wrapped
   wikilink warning `op-commit` does and refreshes the semantic index. A refused or
   failed close (token not open, unreadable `--paths-file`, the guard, a pre-dirty
   path, a git failure) prints a line starting `not committed:` to stderr, exits 1,
   pushes nothing and keeps the token. A close that landed whose sync then failed
   prints a line starting `committed, not published:` with the short sha, exits 1, and
   the token is gone because the commit exists; run `wiki-sync.mjs` again once the
   cause is fixed. Pass `--paths-file` instead of relying on the recorded paths when
   you have also written pages with tools that do not record them.

   Without `--op`, `wiki-sync` also prints, for each open operation that has recorded
   paths still uncommitted, `operation <token> (<op>) has <n> recorded path(s) not
   committed; if it is yours, close and publish it with: node scripts/wiki-sync.mjs
   --op <token>`. It is a line, not a failure: a sync cannot know whose operation it
   is, so the exit code is unchanged and already-committed work is still pushed. It
   follows the once-per-set, once-a-day rule of the open-operations note, keyed by
   token and recorded count, so it is said again when an operation records more. An
   open operation with no recorded paths gets only the existing note.

## Recovery and token ownership

- **Retry the same operation.** After a recoverable failure, inspect the token,
  exact owned files and actual commits before retrying the failed step. Resolve
  an understood cause within the authorized scope without another confirmation.
  A failed Git close keeps its token; retry that `op-commit`, not the edits or an
  already-written log. Never delete a Git lock or guess at a content conflict.
- **Reconcile uncertain completion.** A timeout may have occurred after a commit
  or token removal. Verify the actual commit's subject and path membership, owned
  content and validation state. A completed no-op or already-committed operation
  with a retained token still closes through its own scoped `op-commit`; an empty
  delta alone does not prove completion. If the token is already gone, verify
  closure and continue from the next unfinished step rather than opening a new
  token or replaying work. After a sync rebase, locate the operation through its
  unique log path and recheck the resulting commit instead of relying on its old SHA.
- **Respect holds and ownership.** Do not close a user-held operation. A delegated
  worker reports its owned paths and validation to its enclosing operation's named
  owner rather than closing the parent's token. The hand-off is the ledger: the brief
  gives the worker the parent's token; the worker records each path it writes with
  `op-ledger.mjs add --since <parent token> <path>...` (a clipper it runs takes
  `--since` too) and reports its validation; it never runs `op-commit` or `op-abort`.
  The owner runs `op-ledger.mjs show --since <parent token>`, resolves whatever it
  lists as unclaimed, and closes once. That owner remains responsible for
  the scoped commit, push and remote verification; delegation does not drop the
  publication step. Leave other agents' tokens alone unless ownership was explicitly transferred;
  tokens contain an opening dirty-path snapshot, not proof of who owns later edits.
- **Leave actionable blockers.** If safe progress requires an unresolved conflict,
  missing authorization or another owner's action, retain the operation and record
  its token, owned paths, completed steps, pending work and exact next action. Report
  that blocker or ownership handoff; do not claim completion or silently abandon it.

**Abandoned tokens.** List retained tokens with
`node "<absolute-plugin-root>/scripts/op-cleanup.mjs"` (a dry run). Older than 24
hours means a review candidate, not proven abandonment; these tokens still block
`wiki-sync --commit-local`. For a verified-abandoned operation you own, with no
unfinished work or user hold, apply cleanup with its explicit `--apply --token <id>`
without another approval. Prefer normal `op-commit` closure when the saved operation
can be completed. `--hours <n>` changes the age filter, with a one-hour minimum;
respect that eligibility and verify removal. Never sweep tokens by age or delete
them manually. Token files are local Git-ignored state, not cross-machine locks.
The paths an operation's writers recorded sit in `<token>.paths.jsonl` beside the
token. `op-commit` (when the close lands), `op-abort` and a stale token removed by
`op-cleanup` take it with them; `op-cleanup` also lists a ledger whose token is
already gone and removes it only with `--apply --token <that id>`.

**Stopping early.** A session that opened an operation and will not finish it, or whose work landed another way, drops its own token with `node "<absolute-plugin-root>/scripts/op-abort.mjs" --since <token>`. It removes that one token whatever its age and nothing else: the files the operation wrote stay in the working tree, uncommitted, for a later operation to commit. Do not use it on a token another session holds. Open operations are visible without running a sync: `health` and `session-brief` print a line when any are open, and `wiki-sync` mentions other writers' operations once for a given set of tokens, again when the set changes, and once a day while it stays true.

**Refused sync.** `wiki-sync` refuses to integrate while uncommitted edits overlap files
that the upstream changed: it prints `uncommitted edits overlap incoming changes in
<files>` and exits 3, the one exit code for this refusal (every other failure exits 1).
It changes nothing: no commit, stash or checkout, and the files and open tokens are
untouched. With no operation open the dirty files are hand edits, and the message is that
one line ending `commit them (or finish the operation) and sync again`. With an operation
open the message is longer: one line per overlapping file, `<file>: recorded by operation
<token> (<op>)` when an open operation's recorded ledger names the file and it is still
dirty, otherwise `<file>: not recorded by any open operation`; then `Open operations:
<token> (<op>), ...`; then `If you wrote these edits, finish your operation
(wiki-sync.mjs --op <token>) and sync again.` (the token is filled in only when exactly one
open operation recorded an overlapping file, otherwise the line shows the literal
`<token>`); then `If you did not, leave them exactly as they are:
do not reset, checkout, stash or delete them. Wait for their owner to close the operation, then sync again.` That
last instruction is the rule: a file you did not write is not yours to reset, check out,
stash or delete to get the sync through. Wait, and sync again after its owner closes. The
`recorded by` line is a hint, not proof of ownership. It reads only what writers recorded
with `--since` or `op-ledger.mjs add` (a generated file such as `index.md` is recorded only
when `index-gen` ran with `--since`) and ignores a ledger path that is not dirty now, an
unreadable ledger and the opening snapshot in a token, which says what was already dirty,
not who wrote it. `not recorded by any open operation` therefore does not mean no one is
writing the file. Each refusal also appends a counts-only line to the refusal record below.

**Refusal record.** Each `op-commit` close that is refused and keeps its token, and each
`wiki-sync` that stops on an overlap (see "Refused sync"), appends
one JSON line to `.wiki-master/op-refusals.jsonl` (local, Git-ignored): `at` (ISO
time), `op`, `kind` and `paths`. `paths` is a number and never a path name. `kind` is
`pre-dirty` (a ledger path already dirty before `op-begin` and not adopted; `paths` is
how many), `evidence` (a declared size or hash that does not match what git would store;
`paths` is the size of the evidence map), `unscoped` (the guard; `paths` is how many
delta paths the close would have committed) or `sync-overlap` (`op` is `wiki-sync`;
`paths` is how many files overlap). A close that lands appends nothing, and a
failed append (a directory in the file's place, a read-only disk) changes neither the
message nor the exit code. `health` prints `Recorded refusals: N (pre-dirty a,
evidence b, unscoped c, sync-overlap d).` only when N is above zero, and `health --json`
always carries `opRefusals` as `{ total, preDirty, evidence, unscoped, syncOverlap }`. The
line was `Recorded op-commit refusals: N (...)` in 0.85.0. Like the open-operations line it
sits outside the defect count. The file is never trimmed by the plugin and a line that is
not a record of a known kind counts as nothing.

**Git ownership.** The plugin's scripts make the scoped commits and the sync: `op-commit`
commits what one operation wrote, and `wiki-sync.mjs` pulls, rebases and pushes. A new
vault's `vault-schema.md` (written by `wiki-init`) carries the same statement; an existing
vault keeps its own file. The Obsidian Git plugin stays installed for its source-control
view and for pulling. Its auto-commit and auto-push must be off (auto commit-and-sync
interval 0, commit on file change off, auto push interval 0): they commit half-finished
operation edits under "vault backup" and leave `op-commit` an empty delta. `wiki-sync`
warns when they are on. Every machine sharing the vault needs the same setting. An
instruction elsewhere that says Obsidian Git is the sync engine is stale.

**Done only when** the requested change is validated, applicable catalogs and one
operation log are recorded, the operation commit is verified (or its precise
limitation reported), and its push and remote publication are verified. A user-held
or local-only result must be labeled accordingly. If blocked partway, preserve the
actual operation/commit state and leave the actionable handoff above; a sync failure
after token closure does not require a replacement token. Do not start over blindly.

## Exceptions with their own transaction

**Re-clipping:** `apply-reclips.mjs` applies repairs but does not own a commit. Use an enclosing operation with an exact target list and ownership ledger; inspect its returned changed paths. A verified repair, a pending table verification and a quarantine are distinct outcomes. Quarantine may close triage without making evidence citable. See [re-clipping and quarantine](../../../docs/reclipping.md) for selectors, mode overrides and the explicit terminal-failure policy.

- `purge.mjs --apply`, `--restore` and `--reconcile` own their manifests, logs and
  commits. Do not wrap their transaction in a competing commit. Collateral Markdown
  repairs use an ordinary operation after the purge commit. Keep every seed/plan,
  blocking-source and publication safeguard in the purge skill.
- Fresh `wiki-init` can open an operation before scaffolding: the helper can create
  its state directory before the other folders exist. Without Git, explicitly report
  local-only initialization; do not manufacture a repository or publish it.
- Starting triage UI only creates machine-local session state; it is not a content
  edit and does not need a commit. Applying dispositions that change tracked vault
  content or pipeline state uses an enclosing or new ordinary operation.

## Executable lifecycle templates

Replace absolute path placeholders, title and narrative with the real task. The
comment marks where the already-authorized edits and checks occur; do not run the
close step after a failed edit/check. These examples assume a configured upstream
and no explicit user hold, so they include the push step. For an explicit local-only
request, omit that step and report the unpushed commit. The close is scoped with
`--paths-file`; to close and publish in one command, replace the `op-commit` and
`wiki-sync` lines with `wiki-sync.mjs --op <token> --title 'Task title'` (add
`--paths-file <ledger>` to scope it explicitly).

```powershell
$wikiPriorVault = $env:WIKI_MASTER_VAULT
try {
  $env:WIKI_MASTER_VAULT = 'C:/absolute/path/to/vault'
  $wikiOpToken = node 'C:/absolute/installed/plugin/scripts/op-begin.mjs' --op relink
  if ($LASTEXITCODE -ne 0) { throw 'Could not open wiki operation' }
  # Perform authorized edits, validate, and refresh affected catalogs here.
  # Record each page written with your own file tools: op-ledger.mjs add --since $wikiOpToken <path>...
  'Validated task narrative' | node 'C:/absolute/installed/plugin/scripts/log-entry.mjs' --op relink --title 'Task title' --since $wikiOpToken
  if ($LASTEXITCODE -ne 0) { throw 'Could not log wiki operation' }
  $wikiLedger = Join-Path ([System.IO.Path]::GetTempPath()) "wiki-ledger-$wikiOpToken.json"
  node 'C:/absolute/installed/plugin/scripts/op-ledger.mjs' show --since $wikiOpToken --out $wikiLedger
  if ($LASTEXITCODE -ne 0) { throw 'Could not build the wiki operation ledger' }
  # Read what show listed as unclaimed before closing. An unscoped close is refused while another operation is open.
  node 'C:/absolute/installed/plugin/scripts/op-commit.mjs' --op relink --title 'Task title' --since $wikiOpToken --paths-file $wikiLedger
  if ($LASTEXITCODE -ne 0) { throw 'Could not commit wiki operation' }
  node 'C:/absolute/installed/plugin/scripts/wiki-sync.mjs'
  if ($LASTEXITCODE -ne 0) { throw 'Wiki update is committed locally but not verified published' }
} finally {
  $env:WIKI_MASTER_VAULT = $wikiPriorVault
}
```

```sh
(
  export WIKI_MASTER_VAULT='/absolute/path/to/vault'
  wiki_op_token=$(node '/absolute/installed/plugin/scripts/op-begin.mjs' --op relink) || exit
  # Perform authorized edits, validate, and refresh affected catalogs here.
  # Record each page written with your own file tools: op-ledger.mjs add --since "$wiki_op_token" <path>...
  printf '%s\n' 'Validated task narrative' | node '/absolute/installed/plugin/scripts/log-entry.mjs' --op relink --title 'Task title' --since "$wiki_op_token" || exit

  node '/absolute/installed/plugin/scripts/op-ledger.mjs' show --since "$wiki_op_token" --out "$wiki_ledger" || exit
  # Read what show listed as unclaimed before closing. An unscoped close is refused while another operation is open.
  node '/absolute/installed/plugin/scripts/op-commit.mjs' --op relink --title 'Task title' --since "$wiki_op_token" --paths-file "$wiki_ledger" || exit

)
```

material reused through another wiki page. Even a summary of a single platform
source needs its heading. Raw clippings retain the captured content without rewriting.

do not turn a few comments into consensus, prevalence or established facts.
Disclose missing comments or reply context when the capture is incomplete;
do not claim a full thread was captured without verifying it. Upvotes do not
establish credibility.

sections, opening summary and recommendations. A fact independently supported

any platform comparison stays in its labeled section. Retain all provenance in

## Style: viewpoints whole, conclusions after, breadcrumbs always
Narrative is licensed; dismissal is not. Three house rules govern every page:

1. **Opposing viewpoints appear in their entirety** — in their own strongest
   terms, attributed to their holders — before any conclusion engages them.
   A viewpoint the page ends up arguing against gets the same care as one it
   endorses; weight follows the evidence the vault holds, and no viewpoint is
   waved off by tone (loaded verbs, scare quotes, "supposedly"). When sources
   conflict, keep the claims separate and attributed — never resolve them into
   one synthesized voice that erases the disagreement.
2. **Viewpoints first, conclusions after — and conclusions declare themselves.**
   Every analytic sentence is one of: *inherited* (a source says it — cite it),
   *extended* (built on a source — cite it, mark what's added), or *original*
   (the wiki's own inference — say so explicitly, never state it in the
   page's neutral voice). Joining source A to source B to imply C is an
   *original* claim even when A and B are both cited.

# Relay Trial: Phase/7

This is a controlled evaluation fixture rather than a real field study. In a single controlled relay run, twelve messages were sent with distinct identifiers. Eleven acknowledgements arrived within two seconds. One message timed out at a five-second deadline. Automatic retries were disabled throughout the run. The event log records identifiers, send times, acknowledgement times when present, and the timeout event. The trial does not establish exactly-once processing, durable storage, security properties, or a universal delivery guarantee. A timeout alone does not show whether the receiver received or processed the message. The observed result applies only to this one small fixture run. No comparison against another protocol was performed. For acknowledged delivery, this evidence adds a concrete example of separating receipt observations from claims about successful application processing. Operators reviewing the fixture should preserve that distinction and should not turn eleven acknowledgements into a production reliability claim.

A controlled evaluation fixture, not a real field study ([[raw/clippings/Relay Trial - Phase-7.md]]).

## Observations

- One controlled relay run sent twelve messages with distinct identifiers.
- Eleven acknowledgements arrived within two seconds; one message timed out at a five-second deadline.
- Automatic retries were disabled throughout.
- The event log records identifiers, send times, acknowledgement times when present, and the timeout event.

## Stated limits

The source says the trial does not establish exactly-once processing, durable storage, security properties, or a universal delivery guarantee. A timeout alone does not show whether the receiver received or processed the message. The result applies only to this one small run, and no other protocol was compared. The source cautions against turning eleven acknowledgements into a production reliability claim.
